title: How garbage collection (mark and sweep) works
sub: Start from the things your program can reach, mark everything they touch, then sweep away whatever was never marked. Each step is one object.
aria: A graph of heap objects with roots on the left; objects turn amber then blue as they are marked, then unmarked ones are freed
breakLabel: 💥 Break it: the collector forgets a root
breakOff: Normal run: mark from every root, then free only the unmarked objects.
breakOn: The collector skips root R1, as if a stack variable was missed. Everything only reachable through it never gets marked, so it is freed while the program still points at it.
learn: Roots are where the program can start from: stack variables, globals. An object is live if you can follow references from a root to it.
Mark: white = not seen yet, amber = found but its references not scanned yet, blue = scanned. When no amber is left, every reachable object is blue.
Sweep: walk the heap and free every object that is still white. Garbage can even point at other garbage, or in a cycle, and still gets collected.
Raise References per object: denser graphs mean more of the heap is reachable, so less is freed.
Break it: miss one root and the collector frees objects the program still uses. The red ones are dangling pointers, the root of use-after-free crashes.
Real collectors add tricks (generations, incremental or concurrent marking, write barriers) that are not shown here.
